Use case: stylized-concept. Illustration for "One More Building", a small zombie survival deckbuilder.
Match the supplied existing art EXACTLY: gritty painterly hand-inked graphic novel, rough dark charcoal contours, restrained flat tonal planes, weathered paper/screen-print texture. Muted desaturated concrete greys, dusty off-white, charcoal and at most ONE specified accent colour. Soft low sunlight or overcast light. No glossy surfaces or excessive gradients. NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT cute, NOT anime.
Landscape 3:2, exactly 1536x1024 px PNG, full-bleed, opaque background, no border or frame.
Bold silhouette and strong subject/background contrast, readable at 200px wide.
Mood tense, quiet, lonely and resourceful. No blood, corpses or violence. No people or zombies except the explicitly requested tiny distant hospital silhouette.
STRICT: NO text, letters, numbers, readable signs, logos, watermarks, signatures or UI anywhere. All labels, packages, licence plates and signs completely blank. No close-up faces. No copying an existing franchise, brand or character.
References are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: reproduce their ink, tonal shading and print texture while creating the new subject.
CARD COMPOSITION: One clear object centred, around 60% of image, fully visible with at least 10% calm margin on EVERY side. Close view on a surface, simple faint background. A subtle warm off-white shaft of light suggests a rare found treasure, no extra accent.
ACCENT: danger red #a5312a
SUBJECT: A pump-action shotgun lying across a dusty wooden table, a few shells beside it. No muzzle flash, no person. Neutral grey weapon and table, muted red on shells or a small weapon detail.
FRAMING CORRECTION: Pull the camera back substantially. The ENTIRE shotgun must fit comfortably inside the central 65% of the canvas width, from x=270 to x=1260, with both stock and muzzle far from the edges. Leave broad empty dusty tabletop on the left and right. Do not crop any part of the weapon. The shell cluster is small, secondary and close to its centre. Use a shallow diagonal so the entire silhouette remains inside the wide central image strip.
